whatFailed: Step 8 asserted that GET /api/v2/envelope/item/{itemId}/download?version=signed on a PENDING envelope returns something that is NOT a PDF, and the server returned 200 with the original PDF, which is exactly what the product's own download docs say happens.

docClaim.quote: The API cannot: ... Retrieve the signed PDF until all recipients have completed signing

observed: 200 with Content-Type application/pdf and a 629-byte body beginning %PDF-1.7. The bytes are byte-identical to the version=original download taken in step 6 (same /ID and same @libpdf/core producer block), so the endpoint served the unsigned original upload, not a signed PDF. Steps 6 and 7 both passed; only step 8, which asserts the negation of step 7 about the same request, failed. server.stderr.txt is empty and server.stdout.txt shows no error for the call.
impact: None. The product behaved as documented; the scenario encodes two mutually exclusive assertions about one request, so one of them fails by construction.

notes:
The two doc pages do not actually conflict, which is where the scenario went wrong. first-api-call.mdx says the API cannot retrieve THE SIGNED PDF before completion, which is true: no signed PDF exists yet, because sealing is what produces it. common-workflows.mdx says what the endpoint returns instead, which is the original. The scenario's step 8 note converts 'cannot retrieve the signed PDF' into the much stronger and unpromised 'no PDF comes back at all', then asserts it against the same request step 7 asserts the opposite of. The right corpus action is a conflictResolution on this dispute in favor of common-workflows.md and dropping the fc-api-cannot-retrieve-signed-pdf-before-completion milestone's falsifiable form, not a bug report.

Code confirmation (read, not inferred), tested worktree v2.16.0: apps/remix/server/api/download/download.ts lines 55-128 route version signed/original to handleEnvelopeItemFileRequest, and apps/remix/server/api/files/files.helpers.ts line 112 does `const documentDataToUse = version === 'signed' ? documentData.data : documentData.initialData;`. Before completion documentData.data is still the uploaded original: packages/lib/jobs/definitions/internal/seal-document.handler.ts lines 277-300 create a NEW documentData row for the sealed PDF and repoint envelopeItem.documentDataId at it inside the completion transaction. That is why steps 6 and 7 returned identical bytes. Blame on files.helpers.ts:112 is d05bfa9fe (David Nguyen, 2025-11-07); the surrounding function signature was reshaped by 8c0e029b1 (Ephraim Duncan, 2026-05-05). Both predate the tested tag and neither is a defect.

One genuine, minor observation for a maintainer, not the cause of this failure: on the version=signed path handleStaticFileRequest still sets Content-Disposition to `<title>_signed.pdf` (files.helpers.ts lines 144-150) even when the served bytes are the unsigned original. A caller who trusts the filename rather than checking envelope.status can persist an unsigned PDF under a _signed name. The docs warn about the substitution, so this is a naming wart rather than a contract break; a 200 with the original named `_signed.pdf` and no distinguishing header is the only part of this behavior a doc reader could be surprised by.
